summary.text: Alison Marchant has been the Labor member for Bellarine since the 2022 election, when she succeeded the retiring Lisa Neville. Raised on a farm at Leopold, she taught in primary schools and campaigned against fracking before entering Parliament. She is seeking re-election in Bellarine in 2026.

occupation.text: Primary school teacher; later an electorate officer

priorities.text: Putting the community at the centre of government decisions

sources.title: Alison Marchant, Parliament of Victoria
Alison Marchant, Wikipedia

summary.text: Callum Whitehead is the Liberal candidate for Bellarine at the 2026 Victorian election. He grew up in Shepparton, now lives in Leopold, and has worked in communications and community engagement in the public and private sectors, including on the staff of Liberal and National MPs. He currently serves as president of the Leopold Cricket Club.

prior_roles.role: Staff positions with Liberal and National members of parliament
prior_roles.note: The ABC says he has held such positions but gives no names or years, or whether any continues.

sources.title: Bellarine: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Callum Whitehead, Liberal for Bellarine, Liberal Party of Victoria

summary.text: Dom Williams is standing for Socialist Alliance in Bellarine at the 2026 Victorian election. He studies at Deakin University, has a part-time job as a cleaner, and helped organise School Strike 4 Climate protests while still at high school. He campaigns on climate, public education and the rights of people with disability.

prior_roles.role: Organiser, School Strike 4 Climate (while at high school)

priorities.text: I want the energy industry under public control and increased investment in renewable energies
Paying politicians an average worker's wage
Public education and the rights of people with disability

sources.title: Bellarine: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Dom Williams for Bellarine, Socialist Alliance

previous_candidacies.note: No source says the 2026 candidate is the same person as the 2022 Family First candidate for Bellarine; the name, party and seat all match.

summary.text: Guy Manuell is the Family First candidate for Bellarine at the 2026 Victorian state election. A candidate with the same name ran for Family First in Bellarine in 2022, winning 1,033 first-preference votes (2.2 per cent) without being elected. Neither the party nor the ABC had published a biography as at early November 2026.

sources.title: Bellarine, 2026 Victorian election guide (candidates and 2022 result), ABC News
2026 Victorian State Election candidates, Family First Party
Candidates of the 2022 Victorian state election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Kate Lockhart is standing as an independent for Bellarine at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The ABC links her to the website of her 2025 federal campaign, when she ran as a community independent for Corangamite and won about 4.4 per cent of first preferences. That site describes her as an agricultural scientist who settled on the Bellarine almost 20 years ago, volunteers with Bellarine Landcare and local sports clubs, and received a City of Greater Geelong community award for climate action in 2023.

prior_roles.role: School council member at her daughters' schools

priorities.text: Cost-of-living relief and secure housing (her 2025 federal campaign pledges)
Climate action, gender equity, integrity and transparency, the community independents' platform she ran on in 2025
Better public transport and infrastructure to keep up with population growth on the Bellarine

sources.title: Candidates for Bellarine District, Victorian Electoral Commission
Bellarine, 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

About Kate Lockhart, Vote 1 Kate Lockhart (2025 campaign website)

summary.text: Mitch Pope is the Greens candidate for Bellarine at the 2026 Victorian election. He owns a wholefoods shop with a cafe, works as a photographer, content creator and eco-tour guide, and describes himself as a local community organiser and advocate for the environment and social justice. At the 2025 federal election he stood for the Greens in Corangamite, a federal seat that takes in Bellarine.

occupation.text: Wholefoods store and cafe owner; eco-tour guide, content creator and photographer

priorities.text: tax the big corporations (banks and casinos) to fund universal public services
ban corporate donations to political parties
Action on climate change, affordable housing and the cost of living

sources.title: Bellarine: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Mitch Pope, Candidate for Bellarine, Victorian Greens
Division of Corangamite, Wikipedia

summary.text: Ronan Keogh is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Bellarine at the 2026 Victorian election. He grew up in Townsville, holds a biomedical science degree from Deakin University and has worked as a petrol station sales assistant. His campaign centres on reversing privatisation and on better public transport for the peninsula.

occupation.text: Sales assistant at a petrol station

priorities.text: I believe in a future built by workers, not bosses.
Bringing privatised services such as energy and public transport back under public control, and cutting public spending on private contractors
More and easier-to-use bus routes across the Bellarine, and V/Line services extended onto the peninsula
A public works program to look after and build roads, parks and public buildings
More publicly owned land to protect the natural environment

sources.title: Bellarine: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Ronan Keogh, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Ross McRae is the One Nation candidate for Bellarine at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's election guide says his career has been in technology, covering cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, and that he spent a decade as an IT manager in the Australian Army. Neither the ABC nor any other source we could read had published more about him by November 2026.

prior_roles.note: The ABC gives the length of service but no years, and doesn't say outright that it has ended.

sources.title: Bellarine: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
